title: Vayakhel: too much (Exodus 36:5–7)
hookLine: the people bring so much that Moses asks them to stop

cards: Every fundraiser has the same worry: will enough come in? The school bake sale, the roof appeal, the online campaign with a little bar creeping toward the goal. Now picture the opposite.
The gifts pour in so fast that the people running the project go to the leader and say, please, make them stop. There's too much.
The Torah wrote down that it happened, in the desert, with a camp of former slaves building a sanctuary out of what they carried.

teach.b: Moses has asked for gifts for the sanctuary from everyone whose heart moves them: gold, silver, bronze, blue and purple yarn, linen, goat hair, wood, oil, spices, stones.
The text says they kept bringing, morning after morning.

Then the craftspeople stop their work and come to Moses: the people are bringing much more than enough. So Moses sends word through the whole camp: no man or woman should make anything more for the offering.
And the Torah adds, so the people were held back from bringing. Then one last line, in the JPS 1917 translation: "For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much."
In Hebrew, dayam v'hoter: their enough, and more. How can something be exactly sufficient and also too much?
The eighteenth-century commentator Or HaChaim offers a tender answer: there really was extra, but God made room for all of it in the work, so that no one who gave would see their gift set aside.

teach.h: THE SAME GOLD, A DIFFERENT AIM.
teach.b: The Jerusalem Talmud adds a sharper note: this same people gave their gold for the calf, and gave their gold for the sanctuary. The generosity was the same. What changed was what it was for.
And notice who says stop. Not the givers. The builders.
It takes someone close to the work to see that the need is met, and the honesty to say so out loud, when it would be easy to keep taking.

how: Jewish charity, tzedakah, is often given through communal funds, and the story of the overflowing gifts for the sanctuary is read each year in the portion Vayakhel.

games.q: you're one of the builders. the gifts keep arriving every morning, and you already have everything the work needs. what do you do?
o: keep quiet and store the extra.
tell Moses there's more than enough.
games.why: the builders go to Moses: the people bring much more than enough. Moses tells the camp to stop.

practice: Look around wherever you are, slowly: the food in the kitchen, the clothes in the closet, the hours in the week, the people who love you.
Pick one place where you already have enough, maybe more than enough, and say so to yourself: this is enough. Then let the wanting rest for a breath or two.
